hints: Because $Q$ ($0.7\text{ kg}$) hangs in equilibrium, the string tension is $T = 0.7g = 7\text{ N}$.
Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane to find the normal reaction on $P$: $R = 0.4g\cos\alpha = 0.4(10)(0.8) = 3.2\text{ N}$.
For the greatest value of $X$, impending motion of $P$ is down the plane, so friction acts up the plane: $X + mg\sin\alpha = T + F$.
walkthrough:
Since $Q$ is in equilibrium hanging vertically, the tension in the string is:
$$T = m_Q g = 0.7(10) = 7\text{ N}$$
From $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, the trigonometric ratios are $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$.

Resolve perpendicular to the plane for particle $P$ to find the normal reaction $R$:
$$R = m_P g\cos\alpha = 0.4(10)(0.8) = 3.2\text{ N}$$
The maximum frictional force is:
$$F = \mu R = 0.5(3.2) = 1.6\text{ N}$$

For the greatest force $X$ to maintain equilibrium, $P$ is on the verge of sliding down the plane, so friction acts up the slope:
$$X + m_P g\sin\alpha - T - F = 0$$
$$X + 0.4(10)(0.6) - 7 - 1.6 = 0$$
$$X + 2.4 - 8.6 = 0 \implies X = 8.6 - 2.4 = 6.2\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze hanging particle $Q$ ($m_Q = 0.7\text{ kg}$) in vertical equilibrium:
$$T - m_Q g = 0 \implies T = 0.7 \times 10 = 7\text{ N}$$
Because the pulley is smooth, the tension $T = 7\text{ N}$ is transmitted along the string to pull particle $P$ up the plane.

Using the given slope gradient $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, construct the standard 3-4-5 right triangle:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6, \quad \cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline for particle $P$:
$$\Sigma F_{\perp} = 0 \implies R - m_P g\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$R = 0.4 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 3.2\text{ N}$$

State and evaluate the limiting friction formula:
$$F = \mu R = 0.5 \times 3.2 = 1.6\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the plane:
For the maximum force $X$ that $P$ can sustain without moving, $P$ is on the point of moving down the plane. Thus, friction $F$ opposes downhill motion and acts up the plane:
$$X + m_P g\sin\alpha - F - T = 0$$
Substitute the known values:
$$X + 0.4 \times 10 \times 0.6 - 1.6 - 7 = 0$$
$$X + 2.4 - 8.6 = 0$$
$$X = 8.6 - 2.4 = 6.2\text{ N}$$
This confirms the greatest value of $X$ is $6.2\text{ N}$.

hints: Compare the forces along the plane: tension pulling up is around $7\text{ N}$, whereas the downhill force is $X + mg\sin\alpha = 0.8 + 2.4 = 3.2\text{ N}$. Therefore, $P$ accelerates up the plane.
Because $P$ moves up the plane, friction acts down the slope: $F = 1.6\text{ N}$.
Write Newton's second law for $Q$ descending: $0.7g - T = 0.7a$.
Write Newton's second law for $P$ ascending: $T - X - mg\sin\alpha - F = 0.4a$, then add the equations to solve for $a$.
walkthrough: When $X = 0.8\text{ N}$, the downhill forces on $P$ are $X + m_P g\sin\alpha = 0.8 + 2.4 = 3.2\text{ N}$. Since the hanging weight of $Q$ ($7\text{ N}$) exceeds $3.2\text{ N} + F = 4.8\text{ N}$, particle $P$ accelerates up the plane and $Q$ accelerates downwards.
Because $P$ moves up the slope, friction opposes motion and acts downwards: $F = 1.6\text{ N}$.

Write Newton's second law for both particles:
$$\text{For } Q: \quad 0.7(10) - T = 0.7a \implies 7 - T = 0.7a$$
$$\text{For } P: \quad T - 0.8 - 0.4(10)(0.6) - 1.6 = 0.4a \implies T - 4.8 = 0.4a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate $T$:
$$(7 - T) + (T - 4.8) = 0.7a + 0.4a$$
$$2.2 = 1.1a \implies a = \frac{2.2}{1.1} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the direction of motion:
- Downhill forces on $P$ without friction: $X + m_P g\sin\alpha = 0.8 + 2.4 = 3.2\text{ N}$.
- Downward force on $Q$: $m_Q g = 7\text{ N}$.
Because $7\text{ N} > 3.2\text{ N}$, particle $Q$ accelerates downwards and particle $P$ accelerates upwards along the incline.

Identify the direction of friction:
Since particle $P$ is moving upwards along the plane, friction acts downwards along the plane with magnitude $F = 1.6\text{ N}$.

Apply Newton's second law to each particle:
For particle $Q$ (downwards):
$$m_Q g - T = m_Q a$$
$$0.7 \times 10 - T = 0.7a \implies 7 - T = 0.7a \quad \text{[Equation 1]}$$
For particle $P$ (upwards along incline):
$$T - X - m_P g\sin\alpha - F = m_P a$$
$$T - 0.8 - 0.4(10)(0.6) - 1.6 = 0.4a$$
$$T - 0.8 - 2.4 - 1.6 = 0.4a$$
$$T - 4.8 = 0.4a \quad \text{[Equation 2]}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate string tension $T$:
$$(7 - T) + (T - 4.8) = 0.7a + 0.4a$$
$$7 - 4.8 = 1.1a$$
$$2.2 = 1.1a$$
Divide by $1.1$:
$$a = \frac{2.2}{1.1} = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
